name: Haze-Steppe

civilization.name: The Kessari
civilization.notes: Nomadic herders who follow the seasonal rains across the planet's vast steppes. Their population has declined as the desertification of their world accelerates.

description: Haze-Steppe is a large desert world undergoing slow but accelerating desertification. A permanent amber haze of fine dust hangs over the vast steppes that cover most of the planet's surface, reducing visibility to a few kilometers and tinting everything in warm, golden tones. The steppes are not entirely barren, supporting sparse grassland in regions where seasonal rains still fall, but the green zones shrink measurably each year as the climate dries.

The haze gives the world a soft, dreamlike quality that belies the harshness of conditions on the ground. The air is dry enough to crack skin and parch throats within hours of exposure, and the dust infiltrates every mechanism and seal. When the seasonal rains do come, they arrive as brief, violent downpours that turn the dust to mud and the dry riverbeds into flash-flood torrents. For a few weeks afterward, the steppe blooms with desperate color before the dust reclaims it.

The Kessari have survived on Haze-Steppe for millennia, following the rains in great migratory circuits with their herds of drought-adapted beasts. Their oral histories describe a wetter world with rivers and forests, accounts consistent with geological evidence. Failed terraforming equipment of human origin stands rusting in the northern hemisphere, the remnant of an attempt to reverse the desertification that was abandoned when funding evaporated. The Kessari avoid these machines, considering them cursed.

Haze-Steppe represents a world on the edge. The Kessari civilization is declining as their pastoral way of life becomes untenable in an increasingly arid environment. Reviving the terraforming project could potentially save both the ecosystem and the Kessari, but the original failure has made investors wary. The geothermal energy in the equatorial rift zones could power a renewed effort, if anyone is willing to commit the resources to a world most have already written off.
